      "text": "\nSaintYogaMoose♱ — 04:44\nHey Wuyio\nI have a question as someone who plays OSU longer than I have\nthere are times man where I feel more comfortable playing on HR on jumps and sometimes even SOME alt maps\nand I was wondering if that is a bad thing\nIt feels like I have so much speed in me that turning it on allows me to have less restraint but when I have to retrain that speed for slower and control I cant\nMaybe I just answered my own question actually\nBut was wondering if you ever had that and if you did how did you fixed it as well \nif you don\u0027t mind and you aren\u0027t busy ofc\nSaintYogaMoose♱ — 04:52\nBecause I wont lie, non jump maps are more fun in practice but it isn\u0027t fun when you suck lol\n窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪窪 — 14:41\nMy advice? \nTry to become comfortable in being uncomfortable. it\u0027s the same reason why people call other osu players masochists simply because of their dedication to learn a craft they\u0027re not accustomed to. \nThere isn\u0027t a single defining thing that\u0027s absolute that determines your view on having fun in osu, if any at all. You simply are comfortable and are satisfied with being comfortable - therefore you have fun, OR you want to extend your limits - you become borderline uncomfortable - therefore you\u0027ll have fun AFTER you achieve some goals you set for Yourself. \nThe goal for this game isn\u0027t realistically to have fun (it literally has no incentive for you to have fun given the ranking system). However, you can set your fun by setting and achieving your own goals, no matter how big or small you set them, if achieving them is realistic enough for you, you\u0027ll have fun, when you see you\u0027re approaching that line. \nYou aren\u0027t bound to a single skillset either, and your skillset of your top play doesn\u0027t define you either - aim top play, doesn\u0027t mean you are an aim player - therefore it\u0027s important to find yourself and discover what you\u0027re capable of, just like real life. Some do it without thinking, some do it with a little bit of help of others :)",

      "text": "This is a really insightful conversation between you (or SaintYogaMoose) and Wuyio. It highlights one of the most common hurdles players face in *osu!*—the struggle between relying on raw reaction speed versus developing fundamental reading and finger control.\n\nWuyio gave fantastic **mindset and philosophical advice**. To build off their answer, here is the **mechanical breakdown** of why this is happening to you, why it’s not inherently \"bad\" (but can be a bottleneck), and how to practically apply Wuyio\u0027s advice to fix it.\n\n### Why You Feel More Comfortable on HR (The \"AR Screwed\" Phenomenon)\nWhen you turn on Hard Rock (HR), the Approach Rate (AR) goes up—usually to AR10. At higher ARs, there are fewer objects on the screen at any given time. You stop having to *read* complex patterns and start playing \"whack-a-mole.\" You just react instantly to what appears. \n\nBecause you have good raw aim and speed, this feels \"unrestrained.\" Your brain likes it because it doesn\u0027t have to process dense visual information; it just goes fast. \n\nHowever, when you turn HR off or play slower maps, the AR drops. Suddenly, there are 4, 5, or 6 circles on the screen at once. Because your brain is wired for the \"go fast, react instantly\" speed of HR, you end up clicking circles too early or rushing your aim. You’ve replaced **rhythm reading** with **reaction speed**. \n\n### Is it a bad thing?\nAs Wuyio said, it’s not exactly \"bad\"—you\u0027ve just discovered that your current comfort zone is high AR/reaction-based aim. However, it *is* a bottleneck. If you only ever play fast/HR, your finger control, accuracy, and low-AR reading will atrophy. \n\n### How to Apply Wuyio\u0027s Advice (\"Become comfortable in being uncomfortable\")\nWuyio is telling you that to get good at the non-jump maps you actually want to play, you have to endure the frustration of sucking at them for a little while. Here is how you practically \"retrain\" that speed:\n\n**1. Force Yourself to Play No Mod (and Lower AR)**\nDrop your ego regarding your rank or combo. Play No Mod alt maps, tech maps, and stream maps around AR 8.5 to 9.2. When you see a cluster of notes, force yourself to wait. Don\u0027t just react—look at the approach circles and listen to the music.\n\n**2. Play Lower BPM Maps (Focus on Finger Control)**\nSpeed isn\u0027t just about going fast; true speed requires control. If you can tap 220 BPM but can\u0027t accurately tap a complex 160 BPM alt map, you don\u0027t have finger control, you just have stamina. Dedicate sessions to playing 150-180 BPM maps with complex rhythms. It will feel *very* uncomfortable at first (you will probably get a lot of 100s), but your accuracy will skyrocket once your brain adjusts.\n\n**3. Set Mini-Goals for Fun**\nAs Wuyio mentioned, the ranking system doesn\u0027t reward \"fun.\" If you get frustrated because you suck at non-jump maps, change your definition of success for those sessions. Instead of playing to Full Combo (FC) or get PP, play to:\n*   Get above 95% accuracy on a map you usually get 88% on.\n*   Pass a tech map without failing.\n*   Hit a specific tricky alternate pattern perfectly, even if you miss the rest of the map.\n\nWuyio is completely right: your top plays don\u0027t define you. If you want to learn control and alt-maps, you just have to embrace the temporary discomfort of being a \"beginner\" at that specific skillset again!",
